Yep — **LAX changes the board materially.** With your **$20 Vegas → LAX bus** baked in, Frontier gives us a much better escape route than JetBlue’s ~$291.

| Date | Route | Flight | + $20 bus | Stops |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| **Sat 9/26** | **LAX → MCO** | **$148.46** | **$168.46** | **Nonstop** |
| Sun 9/27 | LAX → MCO | $189.14 | $209.14 | 1 stop |
| Mon 9/28 | **LAX → MCO** | **$178.97** | **$198.97** | **Nonstop** |
| **Tue 9/29** | **LAX → MCO** | **$148.46** | **$168.46** | **Nonstop** |

The **9/26 and 9/29 flights are the standout**: Frontier nonstop, **9:40 PM LAX → 5:36 AM Orlando**, 4h56m. Your effective transportation cost is **$168.46 before any luggage charges**.

That beats what we saw from LAS pretty decisively:

- LAS → JAX: ~$196
- LAS → MIA/FLL: ~$200
- LAS → MCO nonstop: ~$257–268
- **Bus + LAX → MCO nonstop: ~$168**

So yes: **Frontier + LAX is now our primary low-cost lane.** Orlando is also the useful Florida landing point because you're not locked into South Florida if the interviews end up Jacksonville/Tampa/Orlando-side. memcite

And I agree on JetBlue: at **$291**, there’s no reason to force it when we're seeing an effective **$168 Frontier nonstop**.

One caveat: we're counting the Vegas→LAX bus as exactly your **$20**. If that bus doesn't terminate conveniently at LAX and there's another local transfer, we'll add that too rather than hide it.
